title: Alternating configuration spectral sequence for etale sheaf cohomology
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $f:U\to X$ a representable surjective etale morphism from a scheme [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume $f$ is separated, meaning that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For $p\geq0$ let $W_p\subset U^{\times_X(p+1)}$ be the open and closed subscheme complementary to all pairwise equality loci [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers, def-weil-open-immersion]. The permutation group $\mathfrak S_{p+1}$ acts freely on $W_p$. Its orbit sheaf $Q_p=W_p/\mathfrak S_{p+1}$, the fppf sheafification of the orbit presheaf [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification], is an algebraic space. The quotient $\pi_p:W_p\to Q_p$ is a representable surjective etale morphism and a torsor for this constant group, and the induced $g_p:Q_p\to X$ is etale. Let $L_p=(\pi_{p,*}\underline{\mathbf Z})^{\mathrm{sgn}}$, the subsheaf on which a permutation acts by its sign; $L_p$ is etale locally isomorphic to $\underline{\mathbf Z}$, and is trivialized by $\pi_p$. For every abelian sheaf $A$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, there is a natural first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence]
$$E_1^{p,q}=H^q((Q_p)_{\mathrm{et}},g_p^{-1}A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L_p)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad H^{p+q}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A).$$
Cohomology here means right derived abelian-sheaf global sections [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions], and tensor is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor product. For each $m\geq0$ the abutment has a finite filtration $H^m=F^0\supseteq F^1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{m+1}=0$ with $F^p/F^{p+1}\cong E_\infty^{p,m-p}$; each entry stabilizes to its $E_\infty$ value. No quasi-coherence or invertibility of any factorial is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0728, lemma-alternating-spectral-sequence; Tag 0727, lemma-twist, for the sign local system and its local trivialization. Quotient existence and torsor description are the objects used in these statements.

proof.text: Put $E=\mathbf Z[U/X]$ and $K_p=\bigwedge^{p+1}E$, with the contraction and exact augmentation $K_\bullet\to\underline{\mathbf Z}$ supplied by [lem-sfb-etale-cover-trace-koszul-resolution]. By [lem-sfb-etale-configuration-exterior-hom], $W_p$ is open and closed and etale over $X$, its permutation action is free, and $\operatorname{Hom}(K_p,F)$ is naturally the sign subgroup of $\Gamma(W_p,F|_{W_p})$. These identifications apply to every abelian sheaf $F$, not just injectives.

source.place: Tags 0723 and 0726, inputs used in the proof of 0728

proof.text: For $G=\mathfrak S_{p+1}$ the action relation $R=\coprod_{\sigma\in G}W_p\rightrightarrows W_p$ is a scheme: use [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Its projections are etale since each component is an isomorphism; it is a monomorphism into $W_p\times_SW_p$ because a distinct tuple has no nonidentity stabilizer, and its image is an equivalence relation by the action laws. Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient]. Its presheaf $T\mapsto W_p(T)/R(T)$ receives the orbit presheaf $T\mapsto W_p(T)/\mathfrak S_{p+1}$ surjectively: a pair in the image of $R(T)$ is $(\sigma w,w)$ on each member of the finite open and closed decomposition $T=\coprod_\sigma T_\sigma$ given by the components of $R$, so two tuples with the same $R$-class have the same orbit Zariski locally on $T$. Hence both presheaves have the same fppf sheafification, and the quotient of the cited theorem is the stated orbit sheaf $Q_p$; it is an algebraic space, $\pi_p$ is representable surjective etale, and $R\cong W_p\times_{Q_p}W_p$. Thus $\pi_p$ is the required torsor. The map $W_p\to X$ coequalizes the action, so the same universal property gives $g_p:Q_p\to X$. It is etale by [lem-trf-space-etale-source-atlas-detection](3), using the scheme atlas $W_p\to Q_p$ whose composite to $X$ is etale.

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-torsor-character-line] to $\pi_p$ and the sign character. It identifies its $L_\chi$ with the stated $L_p$, proves its local rank one and trivialization on $W_p$, and gives $L_p\otimes L_p\cong\underline{\mathbf Z}$. Associating the three tensor factors makes $T_p(F)=F\otimes L_p$ an additive self-equivalence, since $T_p^2(F)\cong F\otimes(L_p\otimes L_p)\cong F$. By [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] the etale inverse images are compatible with composition and $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ localized at $W_p$ is $(W_p)_{\mathrm{et}}$, so $\pi_p^{-1}g_p^{-1}F\cong F|_{W_p}$, naturally in $F$ and compatibly with each permutation $\sigma$ of $W_p$ over $Q_p$ and $X$. For every $F$ on $X$, this, the character isomorphism for $g_p^{-1}F$ and Step 1 give $$\operatorname{Hom}(K_p,F)\cong\Gamma(Q_p,g_p^{-1}F\otimes L_p).$$ The identifications respect every coefficient map.

Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $A\to I^\bullet$ using [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. For etale $g_p$, use [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] to regard its inverse image as localization at the object $Q_p$ on the enlarged etale site; that model gives the equivalences with the small sites. Restriction to a slice preserves injectives by [new-over-pullback-preserves-injectives], and is exact because restriction preserves kernels and locally surjective sheaf maps. Transport across the additive sheaf equivalences preserves exactness and injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions]. Thus $g_p^{-1}I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution of $g_p^{-1}A$. The same equivalence theorem, applied to the additive self-equivalence $T_p$ of Step 3, shows that $g_p^{-1}I^\bullet\otimes L_p$ is an injective resolution of $g_p^{-1}A\otimes L_p$.

Form the first-quadrant double complex $D^{p,q}=\operatorname{Hom}(K_p,I^q)$, with horizontal differential precomposition by $\partial_{p+1}$ and vertical differential postcomposition by $d_I^q$. They commute by associativity of composition; each squares to zero. Use total differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_v$ as in [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Step 3, applied to each $I^q$ and $d_I^q$, identifies its $p$-th column as a complex with $\Gamma(Q_p,g_p^{-1}I^\bullet\otimes L_p)$. By Step 4 and the injective-resolution definition of right derived global sections [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], its $q$-th cohomology is exactly $H^q(Q_p,g_p^{-1}A\otimes L_p)$.

For fixed $q$, injectivity of $I^q$ makes $\operatorname{Hom}(-,I^q)$ exact: the extension property of [def-sp-injective-resolutions] makes restriction along each monomorphism surjective, while factorization through a cokernel identifies its kernel. Apply this to the short exact image-kernel sequences of the augmented resolution in Step 1. It follows that the augmented row $$0\to\operatorname{Hom}(\underline{\mathbf Z},I^q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(K_0,I^q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(K_1,I^q)\to\cdots$$ is exact. A map from the constant integer sheaf is uniquely its image of $1$, so its first term is $\Gamma(X,I^q)$. Thus horizontal row cohomology is zero in positive degree and $\Gamma(X,I^q)$ in degree zero; this identification commutes with $d_I$.

Apply [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] to $D$. Its row spectral sequence has only the row-cohomology degree $p=0$ column nonzero, by Step 6, and at the next page that column is $H^q(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet))=H^q(X,A)$ by [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. All later differentials vanish for degree reasons. Its finite abutment filtration has a single nonzero graded piece, giving the canonical identification $H^m(\operatorname{Tot}D)\cong H^m(X,A)$. The column spectral sequence has the $E_1$ page computed in Step 5, so it is the asserted spectral sequence. The same double-complex theorem gives $F^0=H^m$, $F^{m+1}=0$, $F^p/F^{p+1}\cong E_\infty^{p,m-p}$ and stabilization of every entry.

source.place: Tag 0725, double-complex spectral sequences and abutment; Tag 0728, final paragraph

proof.text: For a coefficient morphism $A\to B$, [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists] gives a map of injective resolutions and hence a map of the double complexes preserving their filtrations. Two lifts are homotopic by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy], applied to the quasi-isomorphism $A[0]\to I_A^\bullet$. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}(K_p,-)$ carries that homotopy to a vertical column homotopy, so the two maps agree on $E_1$ and therefore on every later page. They also induce the same map on total cohomology: on $D^{p,q}$ multiply the vertical homotopy by $(-1)^p$; horizontal cross terms cancel and its total boundary is the difference of the maps. Identity and composition follow by uniqueness. Consequently the spectral sequence from $E_1$, its filtration, and its abutment are natural in $A$ and independent of the resolution by applying this argument to the identity. This completes every clause without inverting any group order.

tool_uses.why: The finite disjoint union constructs the scheme action relation; a general scheme coproduct is a tool, not a change of unit route.
The general scheme etale-equivalence-relation quotient theorem constructs Q_p and its torsor kernel pair; no other node in this unit states that etale presentation theorem.
The general source-atlas criterion descends etaleness of W_p to Q_p over X.
General sheaf-category enough-injectives theorem used to choose a resolution, unrelated to the geometric unit route.
General enlarged etale-site model realizes a space-valued etale map as localization, so the generic slice restriction theorem applies.
General localization theorem for abelian sheaves gives injective preservation on the enlarged etale site.
General additive-equivalence theorem transports injectives across site models and the tensor-line equivalence.
The standard total complex, signs and filtrations are definitions.
Definition of abelian sheaf cohomology via an injective resolution.
The injective extension property makes Hom into each resolution term exact.
General first-quadrant double-complex theorem gives both spectral sequences and their finite abutment filtrations.
General resolution comparison supplies maps over every coefficient morphism.
General uniqueness of maps into bounded-below injectives gives naturality from E_1 and independence of resolution.

lean.note: The geometry and canonical maps are packaged by ConfigurationQuotient. Sign-line sections are the sign subgroup of maps from the existing free represented sheaf to the constant integers on each localized site. Cohomology is right derived additive global sections. E1, stabilization and the finite abutment filtration are in the functor category, including naturality in every abelian coefficient sheaf. The filtration endpoints use an isomorphic inclusion and a zero subobject, equivalent to top and bottom.
